what_this_is: The pinned identity of the ONE document the STANAG 5527 section in FORMAT_COVERAGE.md was read from, plus every value extracted from it that a ruling rests on, each with the locus inside the document. House style follows fixtures/klv/spec/klv_pin.json, fixtures/cat048/spec/cat048_pin.json and fixtures/cat021/spec/sac_pin.json: an edition number names a DOCUMENT and a SHA-256 names the COPY THAT WAS READ, and those are different claims. The PDF is not committed - see not_committed below.
phase: Phase 1, and a NARROWER Phase 1 than stanag4609's. That one pinned a covering document AND the profile its AGREEMENT clause names, so it could write a row set of 37 rows all saying `not yet`. This one pins the covering document ALONE: ADatP-36 Edition B is not in hand, so there is no row set, no mapping table, no fixture plan, no gap and no proposed field. What exists is a pinned document, the rulings that document supports, one delegation row and one park.

adapter.name: stanag5527
adapter.fixture_directory_status: PROVISIONAL. See fixture_directory_ruling.provisional below. The ADAPTER name is not provisional.
adapter.why_the_two_names_differ: The adapter takes the STANAG's number because the document in hand states no field, no message, no encoding and no identifier - its content pages are AIM, INTEROPERABILITY REQUIREMENTS, AGREEMENT, STANDARD, OTHER RELATED DOCUMENTS, SUPERSEDED DOCUMENTS and the administrative clauses - so there is no NATO document IN HAND whose content could name the adapter. The directory takes the content's name because a directory holds PAYLOADS and a payload is not a standard, which is the same split that puts adapter stanag4676's fixtures in fixtures/nits and adapter stanag4609's in fixtures/klv.

adapter_name_ruling.on_what_evidence: Direct reading of the pinned document, all five pages. It is a covering document: the AGREEMENT clause reads 'Participating nations agree to implement the following standard.' and the STANDARD clause names exactly one, 'ADatP-36, Edition B'. Nothing else in the document is technical.
adapter_name_ruling.how_this_differs_from_the_stanag4609_rul: STANAG 4609's covering-document character was STATED by another document - MISP-2019.1 SS C.1.2, 'a covering document rather than a standalone document'. STANAG 5527's is DEMONSTRATED by direct reading of the document itself, which is the stronger of the two: no second document has to be trusted for the reading to hold.
adapter_name_ruling.precedent_does_not_decide_it: The roster contains both conventions - gmti names the CONTENT of STANAG 4607 while stanag4676 and stanag4609 name the STANDARD carrying the content - so precedent could support either and the documents had to.

rejected.nffi: THE RESERVED NAME, RETIRED. Not rejected on the merits of the name but on the absence of a source. (1) It appears in no document in hand: STANAG 5527 Edition 2 never uses the term - zero occurrences across all five pages of extracted text and zero occurrences of the literal bytes 'NFFI' anywhere in the file, checked at both levels. (2) It has no source in this repository either, and the repository already said so: commit 1b0316b's own message recorded 'NFFI appears nowhere in the repository, so the ordinal table's #9 row is the first and only statement of that reservation', and FORMAT_COVERAGE.md's #9 row said 'nowhere else in this repository. This row is the only statement of it'. A name whose only source is the row that uses it is not a derivation. Retiring it rather than letting it survive by default is the whole point of re-deriving a reserved name from a named source. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED HERE: this record does not state what NFFI stands for, what document defines it, or whether earlier ADatP-36 editions used it. None of that is establishable from any document in hand, and asserting it would be exactly the from-memory claim this phase forbids.
rejected.fft_or_ffts_as_the_ADAPTER_name: The covering document's own framing, and rejected as an ADAPTER name on the document's own words. 'FFTS' names SYSTEMS - the title is 'FRIENDLY FORCE TRACKING SYSTEMS (FFTS) INTEROPERABILITY' - and an adapter does not translate a system. 'FFT' names a CAPABILITY: the INTEROPERABILITY REQUIREMENTS clause reads 'The specific benefits of a FFT capability in NATO are improved overall situational awareness ...'. Neither is a format name. The format's name is whatever ADatP-36 Edition B calls it, and that document is not in hand. The candidate SURVIVES for the directory, where the document does supply a payload noun - see fixture_directory_ruling.
rejected.adatp36: The strongest rejected candidate, because ADatP-36 is the standard that actually carries the content. Rejected because it would name the adapter after a DOCUMENT NOBODY HERE HAS READ. The point of ruling a name from documents in hand is that the name is checkable; adatp36 would be derived from a title, an edition letter and nothing else. It also repeats the rejection `misp` took in the STANAG 4609 ruling - a name taken from a governing document rather than from the thing being translated. And if ADatP-36 Edition B arrives and names the content, that name moves the DIRECTORY, not the adapter: the number is the retrieval key for the agreement, which the document's own NATIONAL RATIFICATION RESPONSE and RESTRICTION TO REPRODUCTION clauses both confirm - national responses are recorded in the NSDD against this STANAG, and NATO standardization documents 'can be retrieved from the NATO Standardization Documents Database (https://nso.nato.int/nso/)'.

fixture_directory_ruling.on_what_evidence: The covering document supplies a payload noun exactly once, in IMPLEMENTATION OF THE AGREEMENT, page '- 1 -' to '- 2 -': 'the NATO nations should add to the current and future national ground forces tracking systems, interfaces to produce/consume FFT data in compliance with the ADatP-36 standard'. The same clause also says 'the FFT services required to enable seamless ADatP-36 information exchange' and 'near real time FFT data exchange between different security domains'. 'FFT data' is the covering document naming the thing that crosses the wire, and a fixture directory is named for what is in it.

rejected.nffi: Retired, no source. Same finding as for the adapter name.
rejected.stanag5527: Would reproduce the bug commit 80b38d1 had to fix - three NITS PDFs sitting in a directory named for the adapter when the directory wanted the content's name. Same rejection stanag4609's directory took.
rejected.adatp36: A directory named after a document, and worse than misp was for klv: the pinned PDF would sit at fixtures/adatp36/spec/nato-stanag-5527-edition-2.pdf, a directory named after a document that is not even the file inside it.
rejected.ffts: Names systems, not payloads. The document's payload noun is 'FFT data', not 'FFTS data'.

considered_and_overruled.the_fast_fourier_transform_collision: 'FFT' has a well-known unrelated sense in signal processing. Named here rather than left for a reader to notice. Overruled: the directory sits under fixtures/ beside ais, adsb, cat021, cat048, gmti, klv, legion, nits, pntmap and tak, every one of which is a defence or aviation data format, and the document's own noun governs the name of the document's own payload. A collision with a term from another field is not a reason to override a term the pinned text supplies.

provisional.why: The payload's name is decided by ADatP-36 Edition B, which is not in hand. A covering document can say what its subject is called; it cannot say what the bytes are called.
what_would_overturn_it: ADatP-36 Edition B in hand naming the on-the-wire payload something other than FFT data - a message-set name, a service name or a schema name - in which case the directory takes that name on the gmti / nits / klv precedent.
ADatP-36 Edition B in hand defining more than one payload shape at this adapter's layer, in which case one directory is the wrong SHAPE and the ruling is a re-scoping rather than a rename.
provisional.what_is_NOT_a_reopen_condition: A preference; the Fast Fourier Transform collision, which is already considered and overruled above; or the arrival of any document other than ADatP-36 Edition B. STANAG 7149 and STANAG 2019 are named by the pinned document as RELATED and neither could decide a payload name.
provisional.what_a_later_move_would_and_would_not_to: It would move the directory and the PLANNED_FIXTURE_DIRS entry in tests/test_cdm_harness.py, which is exactly the map 80b38d1 pinned by a test so that such a move is a deliberate edit rather than a typo. It would NOT move the adapter name: stanag5527 is ruled on the covering document and no content document can unrule it.

adapter_number.on_what_authority: FORMAT_COVERAGE.md's ordinal table, section 'The adapter ordinals, and the reserved-ordinal rule', which is the single authority for the series and is checked against every other site by tests/test_cdm_ordinals.py.
adapter_number.what_changed_in_this_round: #9 was RESERVED for a name with no source. The reservation itself was correct and is now made good: the slot was held for a friendly-force-tracking adapter and a friendly-force-tracking covering document has landed in it. The NAME is what changed - nffi retired, stanag5527 ruled from the document - and the ordinal did not move. Under the reserved-ordinal rule stanag4609 keeps #10, cat048 keeps #11 and the cat034 forecast keeps #12; nothing else in the series moved, which is the rule working rather than the rule being applied again.
adapter_number.consequence_for_the_table: No row in the ordinal table is RESERVED any more. #9's state is now 'specification, Phase 1' - the same state string #10 carries - and the reserved-ordinal RULE still stands, because it is the rule that gave #10 to stanag4609 rather than #12 and that held #9 open long enough for this document to arrive.

document: NATO Standardization Agreement (STANAG) 5527, Friendly Force Tracking Systems (FFTS) Interoperability / Interoperabilite des systemes de suivi des forces amies
tasking_authority: DIGITAL POLICY COMMITTEE (DPC), Navigation and Identification Capability Panel (CaP 2)
review_clause: This STANAG is to be reviewed in accordance with AAP-03. The result of the review is to be recorded within the NSDD.
security_classification_statement: This STANAG is a NATO non-classified document to be handled in accordance with C-M(2002)60.
additional_information_page: Page '- ii -' carries one word of content under ADDITIONAL INFORMATION / INFORMATIONS SUPPLEMENTAIRES: 'None.' / 'Aucune.' Below it is the Director NSO signature block. That page is a flattened insert and BOTH its columns extract with dropped characters - the English column comes out as 'Thierry POU LET TE / Major Gen rai, FRA (A) / Director, NATO tandardization Office' and the French as 'ETTE / ion, FRA (A) / ureau OTAN'. The signature is legible enough to identify the office - Director, NATO Standardization Office - and the personal name is NOT recorded here as a verified reading, because reconstructing dropped characters is a guess and no ruling depends on it.
page_layout: Five leaves. Page 1 the bilingual title page, unnumbered. Page 2 the Letter of Promulgation, printed '- i -'. Page 3 ADDITIONAL INFORMATION / INFORMATIONS SUPPLEMENTAIRES with the Director's signature block, printed '- ii -'. Pages 4 and 5 the agreement itself, printed '- 1 -' and '- 2 -'. The document states four page numbers about itself and has five leaves, which is the cross-check the page count was validated against.
bilingual: English and French in parallel columns throughout. Pages 1, 2, 4 and 5 extract cleanly in both languages and are what every quotation in this record is read from. Page 3 is the exception and is recorded in additional_information_page below: it is a flattened insert whose extraction drops characters in both columns, and no ruling rests on it.

the_normative_act.aim: The aim of this NATO standardization agreement (STANAG) is to respond to the following interoperability requirements.
the_normative_act.interoperability_requirement: To provide friendly ground force information throughout the NATO Command Structure, within the respective chain of command, and to increase situational awareness of the land battle space. The specific benefits of a FFT capability in NATO are improved overall situational awareness, improved command and control, force multiplication, improved synchronization of forces, and reduced risk of fratricide.
the_normative_act.agreement: Participating nations agree to implement the following standard.
the_normative_act.other_related_documents: STANAG 7149 - NATO MESSAGE CATALOGUE - APP-11; STANAG 2019 - NATO JOINT MILITARY SYMBOLOGY - APP-06
the_normative_act.implementation_of_the_agreement: To properly take advantage of the standard, the NATO nations should add to the current and future national ground forces tracking systems, interfaces to produce/consume FFT data in compliance with the ADatP-36 standard and should augment the current and future Command and Control systems with interfaces to consume the track position information provided in compliance with the ADatP-36 standard. Nations should also plan for the development and deployment of the FFT services required to enable seamless ADatP-36 information exchange and so ADatP-36 enabled security devices to enable the near real time FFT data exchange between different security domains.
the_normative_act.what_it_contains_that_is_technical: Nothing. The document states no field, no message, no encoding, no identifier, no layout and no requirement of its own. Its only normative act is the AGREEMENT clause, and that clause's entire content is the name of another document. Counted rather than asserted: across five pages the word 'shall' occurs four times - once in the promulgation letter's ACTIONS BY NATIONS clause, once in NATIONAL RATIFICATION RESPONSE, and twice in IMPLEMENTATION OF THE AGREEMENT and FEEDBACK - and not one of the four governs a data element. Every 'should' (three, all in IMPLEMENTATION OF THE AGREEMENT) is advice about national procurement.

delegation.what_this_is: One row, because the AGREEMENT clause names one standard. The version and requirement loci are separated on the convention the STANAG 4609 delegation table set, and for its reason: a reader who takes a version from the requirement that mandates the document can get no version at all.

entries.version_suffix: NONE. 'Edition B' is an edition letter and no version, revision or date accompanies it anywhere in the five pages. This is the AEDP-12 shape - that document is cited elsewhere in this repository as 'Edition B Version 2' - so an edition letter alone does not identify a text, and which version of Edition B is intended is not determinable from this document.
entries.where_the_version_is_stated: The STANDARD clause, page '- 1 -', verbatim: 'ADatP-36, Edition B'. That is the ONLY place in the document where the edition letter appears - twice, in the English and French columns of the same clause.
entries.unsuffixed_at_the_requirement: Yes, and more than unsuffixed. ADatP-36 is named nine times across the document. Exactly two of those nine carry the edition letter, and they are the English and French halves of the STANDARD clause. The other seven - all in IMPLEMENTATION OF THE AGREEMENT - are bare 'ADatP-36' with neither an edition nor a version.
entries.required_by: The AGREEMENT clause, page '- 1 -', verbatim: 'Participating nations agree to implement the following standard.' The STANDARD clause immediately below it is the naming; the AGREEMENT clause is the requirement.
entries.governs: Everything an adapter would need. Every field, message, encoding, identifier and service of Friendly Force Tracking is in ADatP-36 and none of it is in the covering document.

named_as_related_and_explicitly_NOT_dele.why_the_distinction_is_recorded: Both appear under OTHER RELATED DOCUMENTS and neither appears in the AGREEMENT. The AGREEMENT clause names exactly one standard, so exactly one document is delegated to. Filing a related document as a delegation would overstate what the nations agreed to implement, and it is the kind of overstatement a later reader cannot detect without the pinned copy.

entries.version: None stated. No edition and no version accompany either the STANAG number or APP-11.
None stated. No edition and no version accompany either the STANAG number or APP-06.

parks.how_many: One park over one document, and that is the whole of what this phase is waiting for.

park_1.why_it_is_the_only_one: The AGREEMENT clause names one standard and nothing else in the document is technical. There is no second document whose absence costs anything, because there is no content to be missing pieces of.
park_1.what_it_blocks: Everything except the pin, the two names and this record. No row set, no mapping table, no fixture, no fixture plan, no gap, no proposed field and no ambiguity register - a register reads a text, and the text this adapter would read is not here.
park_1.reopen_condition: Obtain ADatP-36 EDITION B specifically - the exact edition the STANDARD clause names, not 'the current ADatP-36'. That is the same exit condition the twelve KLV parks carry and it exists for the same reason: a later revision decoded against an earlier citation is a plausible answer to the wrong question. The edition letter alone does not identify a text either, so a copy in hand must also settle which version of Edition B it is. LAST CHECKED 2026-09-03 and it remains unmet. THE CHECK IS PARTIAL AND SAYS SO: the route this park's own `route` field prints is the NATO Standardization Documents Database, and nso.nato.int answered HTTP 403 at 2026-09-03T10:25:25Z on all six paths asked - the apex, /nso/nsdd/, main/standards, listpromulg.html and two stanag-details pages - with and without a browser User-Agent. The OTHER half of that clause, 'or through your national standardization authorities', IS NOT A ROUTE A PROBE CAN ASK, which is what honest_strength already says: this park closes on an ACCESS decision. So the date records that the machine-askable half was asked and refused, and it does not claim the park was tested end to end. Dated on rule 12's first sweep, which found this field stating a blocker in the present tense with no instant behind it.
park_1.route: The pinned document's own RESTRICTION TO REPRODUCTION clause prints the route for NATO standardization documents: 'They can be retrieved from the NATO Standardization Documents Database (https://nso.nato.int/nso/) or through your national standardization authorities.' That clause is about NATO standardization documents generally rather than about ADatP-36 by name, which is why this is recorded as the document's stated route and not as a confirmed availability.
park_1.honest_strength: Weaker than eleven of the twelve KLV parks and stronger than the twelfth. The MISB parks are public downloads and SMPTE ST 336 needs a purchase decision. This one is neither: NSDD access is by national standardization authority, so the park closes on an ACCESS decision rather than on an afternoon or a budget. || CORRECTED 2026-09-03: THE COMPARISON'S OTHER END HAS MOVED. This field ranked NSDD access between twelve MISB parks that are public downloads and a thirteenth, SMPTE ST 336, that needed a purchase decision. ST 336 turned out to be a free download from SMPTE's own library, park 8 closed on 2026-09-03, and ALL THIRTEEN KLV PARKS ARE NOW PUBLIC DOWNLOADS. So this park is weaker than every one of them rather than weaker than twelve and stronger than one, and the sentence above is a dated record rather than a live ranking. WHAT IS UNCHANGED IS THIS PARK'S OWN STRENGTH: NSDD access still runs through a national standardization authority, which is neither an afternoon nor a budget, and the reason this park was described by contrast is that it has no obvious peer. It still has none.

classification_contingency.why_this_is_here: Obtaining ADatP-36 Edition B and landing a pin were assumed to be one act. They may not be one act, and the branch is written before the fact that decides it so that the round which lands that fact is execution rather than deliberation.
classification_contingency.the_doubt_and_its_provenance: A third-party standards index - GlobalSpec - lists TWO ADatP-36 records: one carries a NATO RESTRICTED marking and one, matching Edition A, carries none. WHICH EDITION THE MARKING ATTACHES TO IS NOT ESTABLISHED.
classification_contingency.what_is_NOT_asserted: Nothing in this record asserts that ADatP-36 Edition B is classified, and nothing asserts that it is not. A reseller index is not the promulgating authority and its markings are not that authority's; two records with one marking between them is as consistent with a catalogue artefact as with a fact about the text.
classification_contingency.the_deciding_fact: The NSDD classification line on the ADatP-36 Edition B record itself. NOT IN HAND.

branch_u_unclassified_or_public.label: Branch U - Edition B unclassified or public.
branch_u_unclassified_or_public.what_lands: The plan above, unchanged. The copy goes to fixtures/fft/spec/, untracked like every other pinned standard in this repository.
branch_u_unclassified_or_public.what_is_recorded: A pin: identity, SHA-256, byte count, page count and local_path - the record shape this file already carries for STANAG 5527 Edition 2.
branch_u_unclassified_or_public.what_the_row_set_rests_on: Quotations, as every other row set in FORMAT_COVERAGE.md does.
branch_u_unclassified_or_public.how_the_gate_sees_it: The pin set derived by tests/test_cdm_pins.py, under that module's closure assertion against the PDFs on disk.

branch_r_nato_restricted.label: Branch R - Edition B NATO RESTRICTED.
branch_r_nato_restricted.what_lands: None of the document's bytes. No PDF in the working tree, not even untracked.
branch_r_nato_restricted.what_is_recorded: Promulgation identity, edition, date and the NSDD classification line. NO HASH - a hash of content this repository may not redistribute is a measurement of a copy it may not hold.
branch_r_nato_restricted.what_the_row_set_rests_on: Clause citations: numbered clauses this repository can name but not reproduce. A reader holding their own lawful copy can check every row against it; a reader without one can see which clause each row rests on and no more.
branch_r_nato_restricted.the_two_names: Settled on receipt, identically to Branch U. Reading a document and carrying it are different acts, and only the second is what this branch forgoes.
branch_r_nato_restricted.how_the_gate_sees_it: The CITED CLASS in tests/test_cdm_pins.py - a node carrying "cite_not_carry": true, asserted disjoint from the pin set in both directions, forbidden to carry sha256, bytes, pages or local_path, and failing loudly if the named document grows bytes anywhere under fixtures/. Legal and empty today.
branch_r_nato_restricted.precedent: FORMAT_COVERAGE.md's NITS pin table, the row labelled 'SHA-256 (2014)': AEDP-12 Edition A Version 1, May 2014, whose bytes are 'Not present in fixtures/nits/spec/'. Commit 3e0aed0 recorded that row as 'the one line in this pin table that the re-verification below could not check', and commit 844e336 cites the same treatment by name - 'Not "outside the repository", the AEDP-12 Edition A (2014) treatment' - as the precedent it DECLINED for the 22 CAT048 editions.
branch_r_nato_restricted.precedent_inverted: There the bytes are outside the tree because a watermarked reseller copy is not reproducible, and the recorded hash is a premise nobody else can check - an accident, recorded honestly. Here the bytes would be outside the tree because they may not lawfully be inside it, and the entry would carry no hash at all, which removes the very thing that made the AEDP-12 line a defect. Deliberate here, defective there, and the two look identical from a file listing.

what_the_nsdd_visit_must_return: The classification line on the ADatP-36 Edition B record - the statement that decides the branch, read off the promulgating authority's own record and not off any index.
Which version of Edition B the copy is - the fact this park already required, because an edition letter alone does not identify a text.
classification_contingency.a_visit_that_returns_neither_fact: leaves this park exactly where it is, document in hand or not.

searched_and_not_found.method: Two passes. (1) Filename patterns - adatp, 36, 5527, nffi, fft, friendly - across all 1321 entries. (2) A content pass over every PDF in the directory, 675 of them, matching the first three pages of extracted text against /ADatP\s*-?\s*36|Friendly\s*Force|NFFI/i.
searched_and_not_found.method_validated: The content pass was validated by its known positive before its negative result was trusted: it found 5527EFed02.pdf, the covering document itself, which is the only file in the directory that contains the term. A search that had found nothing at all would have been a broken search rather than an absent document.
searched_and_not_found.result: ADatP-36 is NOT present in any edition. Neither are STANAG 7149 / APP-11 or STANAG 2019 / APP-06, and neither is any document using the term NFFI.
searched_and_not_found.one_neighbour_worth_naming: 5527EFed02.pdf is the source of the pinned copy and was already named in fixtures/klv/spec/klv_pin.json's own not-found search, which is where this round started.

page_count_method.how: The page objects REACHABLE FROM THE CATALOG'S /Pages TREE, walked in /Kids order.
page_count_method.why_it_is_recorded: A page count is a pin value like any other, so the method that produced it has to be reproducible.
page_count_method.validated_before_it_was_trusted: Run against the NINE documents whose page counts FORMAT_COVERAGE.md already records - eurocontrol-cat048-part4-edition-1-32.pdf 64, nato-aedp-4607-1-edition-a-v1.pdf 212, nato-aedp-4607-edition-a-v1.pdf 104, nato-stanag-4607-edition-4.pdf 6, nato-aedp-12-1-edition-a-v1.pdf 192, nato-aedp-12-edition-b-v2.pdf 150, nato-stanag-4676-edition-2.pdf 5, nato-stanag-4609-edition-5.pdf 5, misb-misp-2019-1.pdf 73 - and reproduced all nine exactly. That is the seven the klv pin validated against plus the two the klv pin itself added.
page_count_method.cross_checked_against_what_the_file_stat: The document prints four page numbers - '- i -', '- ii -', '- 1 -', '- 2 -' - on its second through fifth leaves, with an unnumbered title page first. Four printed folios plus one unnumbered leaf is five, which agrees with the page tree. This is the stronger of the two checks because it does not depend on the tool.
page_count_method.ruling: Ruled in FORMAT_COVERAGE.md, 'The page count, ruled from what a reader does with the number'. A page count is one term of a pin's identity row and its job is to let someone holding a copy check they hold the same document - which they do by opening it and seeing how many pages it has. So the count is the number of pages the document HAS, which is the page tree; a raw-object scan counts FILE OBJECTS, a different quantity that coincides only when a file has no orphaned page objects and no incremental update.
page_count_method.what_this_record_used_to_say_and_why_it_: It used to read: 'Counted from the PDF's own page tree - occurrences of /Type /Page across raw objects and across every inflated object stream. This file keeps its page objects inside compressed object streams, so the inflation path is the one that produced the count.' That sentence names the PAGE TREE and then defines a RAW-OBJECT SCAN, which are two different methods; it was self-contradictory from the day it was written and nothing noticed, because the two agree on any file with no orphaned page objects and no incremental update. CAT034 Phase 1 found the first file where they disagree and recorded the divergence; the harmonisation round ruled for the page tree and rewrote this field. THE COUNTS IN THIS RECORD DID NOT MOVE - both methods give them - so this is a correction to the description of how they were obtained and not to the values.
page_count_method.recomputed_under_the_ruling: Every document in this repository with a recorded page count was recomputed under both methods: 11 pins, 3 CAT034 lineage editions, 22 CAT048 lineage editions. No pin moved. Three CAT048 LINEAGE entries moved - editions 1.28 and 1.29 from 58 to 56, edition 1.30 from 59 to 57 - and cat048_pin.json records each as a correction with the ruling cited.
page_count_method.a_disagreement_found_outside_this_row_se: WITHDRAWN on 2026-08-26, and recomputed_under_the_ruling stands unqualified. This field used to open 'AND THE FIELD BELOW IS FALSE, at one document' and report that fixtures/cat062/spec/eurocontrol-asterix-cat062-p9-appendix-a-ed13.pdf is recorded as 25 pages while the ruled method gives 23, with objects 1760 and 1782 as orphans whose reachable /Parent does not list them and with the file's own top /Pages node stating /Count 23. Re-measured from the bytes in the CAT062 correction round, SHA-256 recomputed first and unchanged at fe7a0deb972dfa87dc0bd2e3c308a6a4fd83f7a9867d334a50daff26cfa3df0e: the ruled method gives 25, the page-tree root's declared /Count is 25, a raw-object scan across the file and every inflated object stream gives 25, no page object is unreachable from the tree, and the pin at 25 stands. THE 23 HAS A NAME: it is a SUPERSEDED GENERATION of the page tree, read as if it were current. The file is linearized and then INCREMENTALLY UPDATED once - three %%EOF markers, the original body ending at the 247816 bytes the linearization dictionary declares as /L - and that update redefines exactly three objects, all of them page-tree nodes, inside object stream 1805 at offset 1078590. The superseded generation, in object stream 80 at offset 246459 in the pre-update body, is 1723 /Count 23, 1724 /Count 5 /Kids [1731 1 7 9 12] and 1727 /Count 8 /Kids [43 45 47 49 51 53 55 57]. The generation the xref chain actually names is 1723 /Count 25, 1724 /Count 6 /Kids [1760 1731 1 7 9 12] and 1727 /Count 9 /Kids [43 45 47 49 51 53 55 57 1782]. A walk that takes an object's FIRST definition in file order rather than the one the xref chain resolves to reads the superseded tree, counts 23 leaves, and reports the two pages the update ADDED as orphans - which is the reading that was recorded here. Both added pages are real pages: A4 /MediaBox 595.32 x 841.92, with 11 355 and 805 bytes of decoded content stream.
